extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys facing or studying USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules used to evaluate alleged professional misconduct by persons practicing before the USPTO, including burdens of proof, duties of practitioners (candor, client funds, communications, filings), and sanctions/procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authority to regulate and discipline practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO has the "exclusive authority to establish qualifications for admitting persons to practice before it, and to suspend or exclude them from practicing before it." This authority flows from 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 35 U.S.C. § 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: Kroll v. Finnerty, Sperry v. Fla. ex rel. Fla. Bar. Statutory basis authorizes USPTO to establish regulations governing conduct of patent attorneys and agents and to discipline practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of the Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations governing the conduct of USPTO practitioners are the Rules of Professional Conduct codified at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 to 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of these rules form the substantive basis for disciplinary counts; practitioners are judged against these regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rules for disciplinary hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary hearings are conducted in accordance with the procedural rules at 37 C.F.R. part 11 and with section 7 of the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. § 556, by an impartial hearing officer appointed by USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific implementing regulations cited include 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.39 and 11.44; procedures include notice and opportunity for hearing as required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard and burden of proof: clear and convincing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director has the burden of proving any alleged violations by clear and convincing evidence, and the respondent bears the burden of proving any affirmative defenses by clear and convincing evidence. (37 C.F.R. § 11.49.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision defines 'clear and convincing' as an intermediate standard requiring evidence that 'produces in the mind of the trier of fact a firm belief or conviction' or proves facts 'highly probable.' Cases cited: Jimenez v. DaimlerChrysler Corp.; Colorado v. New Mexico.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of honesty and candor (no false statements or fabrications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not make false statements or fabricate documents or evidence (e.g., false hospitalization claims, forged 'Acknowledgement Receipt').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the record: documents that did not corroborate claimed hospitalization dates, an 'Acknowledgement Receipt' that appeared forged, and other inconsistent/false representations; tribunal may find lack of candor and impose sanctions or referrals for dishonesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to safeguard client funds and use client trust accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance payments and client funds must be handled appropriately (e.g., deposited into a client trust account rather than an account holding the practitioner's own funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record shows multiple instances where advance payments were not deposited into a client trust account (e.g., payments from Mr. Garczynski and Ms. Kemp placed into an account holding respondent's own funds). Mismanagement of client funds is cited as misconduct in prior disciplinary records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to communicate and notify clients of important USPTO actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must timely notify clients of Office Actions, Notices of Publication, and other correspondence from USPTO that affect the clients' rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Respondent failed to send Ms. Kemp copies of an Office Action and Notice of Publication; purported emails/documents claiming to have notified the client were shown by forensic analysis to be likely unsent or altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to return client files and effect proper transition upon termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination of representation, the practitioner must provide complete copies of client files and otherwise effect an orderly transition; failing to return files is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, respondent did not produce requested files despite a court order and claimed to have transmitted transition materials that the client never received; first production of some documents occurred only during litigation or disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide competent, diligent, and timely representation (including filings and responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must competently manage matters, timely prepare and file applications, respond to Office Actions, file required documents (e.g., power of attorney), and avoid introducing new matter after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: alleged failures to file provisional or non‑provisional applications as represented, failure to file or respond to Office Actions, failing to substitute counsel or file powers of attorney, and misleading explanations about filing mechanics (e.g., claims that a filing receipt is not issued if fee not paid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to maintain accurate and honest billing records
rubrics_metrics.description: Billing must be accurate and not contain fraudulent charges or misrepresentations of time; submitting fraudulent bills is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records referenced include bills that were fraudulent or contained misrepresentations (e.g., charging for time purportedly spent with a client while the client was hospitalized). Discrepant invoices in the record also raised concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide accurate legal advice on IP procedural matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must give accurate guidance on IP procedures (for example, trademark recording procedures and inventorship rules) and must not make misleading statements about how USPTO processes operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Respondent inaccurately stated that USPTO procedures do not allow trademark owners to file licenses (contrary to TMEP § 503.02) and gave misleading advice about inventorship (MPEP § 2137.01(II) governing contribution to conception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with tribunal orders, discovery, and prehearing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must comply with prehearing orders (e.g., identify anticipated exhibits and witnesses, produce exhibits by deadlines) and discovery obligations; failure may prompt motions to compel and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record: respondent failed to identify witnesses or submit exhibits by deadlines, failed to comply with an Order to Compel, and the OED Director filed a Motion for Sanctions; Tribunal granted partial summary judgment and later granted sanctions in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and sanctions for misconduct (including referral and potential suspension/exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If misconduct (such as false statements or other violations) is found, the Tribunal may sanction the practitioner, refer conduct to the OED Director, and such actions can lead to suspension or exclusion from practice before USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Tribunal found false statements about hospitalization and sanctioned respondent by referring conduct to the OED Director; sanctions were sometimes held in abeyance to allow opportunity to show cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and evidentiary procedures when respondent fails to appear
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent fails to appear at an evidentiary hearing, the Tribunal may receive admitted exhibits and witness testimony in the respondent's absence and may close the record and proceed to decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record: respondent failed to appear at the hearing; Tribunal admitted numerous Government exhibits and witness testimony, closed the evidentiary record, and set deadlines for post-hearing briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to produce credible, corroborated documentary evidence (avoid forged/altered documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents produced in defense or to corroborate actions must be authentic and corroborated; forged or doctored documents (or documents with metadata inconsistent with purported dates/senders) undermine credibility and support findings of misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED engaged a digital forensics expert who found Outlook/PDF files had metadata showing creation dates inconsistent with claimed transmission dates and lacked essential metadata indicating they had been sent; an 'Acknowledgement Receipt' had fields missing or mismatched and appeared forged.
